item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q006_ubiquitin_like_function_divergence","answer":"SCOPe supports an evolutionary relationship accompanied by functional divergence. In release 2.08, Ubiquitin-related proteins (family d.15.1.1; SUNID 54237), UBX domains (family d.15.1.2; 54250), and Ras-binding domains, RBD (family d.15.1.5; 54263) are distinct families within the Ubiquitin-like superfamily (d.15.1; 54236). They share the beta-Grasp (ubiquitin-like) fold (d.15; 54235), in the Alpha and beta proteins (a+b) class (d; 53931). Their shared superfamily expresses SCOPe's inference of probable common ancestry; fold or class membership alone would not establish homology.\n\nBiologically, this links a conserved structural scaffold to different roles: ubiquitin and some related modifiers undergo covalent conjugation, many UBX domains bind the p97/VCP/Cdc48 ATPase as adaptor modules, and RBDs mediate interactions with Ras-family GTPases in signaling. These functions are not interchangeable, and not every ubiquitin-related domain is a conjugatable modifier. It would be unsafe to annotate a UBX domain or RBD as a ubiquitin-like covalent modifier, assign ubiquitination or proteasomal targeting to every superfamily member, or transfer Ras-binding or p97-binding specificity across these families solely from their structural classification. Specific functional assignments require independent sequence and interface conservation, domain-context evidence, and relevant biochemical interaction or conjugation evidence. A shared scaffold can guide structural comparison or core-template selection, but does not establish conserved binding surfaces, partners, or mechanisms.","evidence_used":["Pretrained biological knowledge","mcp__scope__search_scop","mcp__scope__get_scop_node","mcp__scope__list_scop_children","/api/v1/releases/current","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=Ubiquitin&mode=auto&limit=30","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=UBX&mode=auto&limit=10","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=Ras-binding&mode=auto&limit=10","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/d.15.1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/d.15.1/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/d.15.1/children?limit=30"]}]}
